thread.title: McGregor Officials Address Gas Line Strikes Amid Internet Expansion
thread.title_full: McGregor Officials Address Gas Line Strikes Amid Internet Expansion

author: Priyanka Patel
title: McGregor Officials Address Gas Line Strikes Amid Internet Expansion
text:
MCGREGOR, Texas (2025-08-28 01:27:00) – Fiber internet installation crews have repeatedly struck gas and water lines across McGregor in recent weeks, raising important safety concerns and drawing responses from city officials and Atmos Energy.
Fiber installation sparks utility line damage concerns in McGregor Construction mishaps have led to multiple gas and water line strikes in McGregor.
City officials and Atmos Energy have confirmed multiple incidents. McGregor plans to continue working with Astound Fiber, which has adjusted its approach. The city of McGregor is experiencing a noticeable increase in struck gas lines. “We’re trying to protect ourselves, our people and our lines,” stated McGregor City Manager Kevin Evans. These incidents are primarily attributed to construction crews from Astound Fiber, the company tasked with installing a fiber-optic network intended to bring high-speed internet to nearly 2,000 homes and 160 businesses.Evans noted,”They came in with a lot of crews,it was actually a little more than we could keep up with.” Posts from the McGregor Volunteer Fire Department’s Facebook page illustrate several gas line strikes, including one incident behind McGregor High School.
McGregor gas lines One local resident expressed frustration: “This is getting ridiculous. This company needs to get it together.”
Atmos Energy confirmed its response to several of these incidents. The company stated, “A construction crew doing work unrelated to Atmos Energy has been working in McGregor and damaged a natural gas pipeline on several occasions over the past week.In each case,Atmos Energy’s highly trained technicians were on scene to make the necessary repairs and restored natural gas service as safely and efficiently as possible.”
Did you no? The most common cause of outside natural gas leaks is digging or construction that disturbs natural gas pipelines.
Atmos Energy also emphasized the importance of calling 811 before digging. “If you nick, scrape, or dent a natural gas pipeline, call 911 and then call Atmos Energy’s emergency number at 866-322-8667,” the company advised. “Even minor damage can weaken a pipeline and lead to a future leak.” State laws require calling 811 a few business days before excavation to notify utility companies.
Regarding the McGregor incidents, the city reported that two of the struck lines were mismarked, and one was a private line with an unknown location. Despite these issues, McGregor has no current plans to halt work with Astound Fiber.
Evans added, “I think the company has adjusted the way they work. we’re working with them, they’ve been very good at adjusting and taking care of damages and trying to work with us ahead of time.” The city will continue to closely monitor Astound’s work.
